tickets.title: Service Running but Management Console is Red
tickets.summary: DHCP has been installed on a new Domain Controller (DC-02). The service is 'Started' in Services.msc, but the DHCP console shows a red down arrow, and no clients are receiving IPs.
artifact: Console: IPv4 node shows a red down arrow icon
Event Viewer: System Log shows Event ID 1046
validations: Verify server appears in 'Authorized Servers' list.
tickets.debrief: In an Active Directory environment, the DHCP service performs a security handshake. It checks AD to see if it is 'Authorized.' If it is not on the whitelist, the service will remain in a dormant state even if the process is 'Running.' This prevents unauthorized 'rogue' servers from disrupting the network.

triage.q: The service is running but the console is red. What is the most professional next step to uncover the specific block?
options: Restart the server to see if the icon clears
Check the System Event Log for Event ID 1046 (Authorization check)
Delete the DHCP role and reinstall it via PowerShell
Ping the loopback address to check the NIC

diagnosis.q: Event 1046 states: 'The DHCP service is not authorized to start.' What does this indicate?
options: The server has a duplicate IP address on the network
The DHCP server has not been granted permission to operate within the AD Forest
The firewall is blocking Port 67
The DHCP Administrators group has been deleted

fix.q: How do you resolve this 'Unauthorized' state in the console?
options: Add the server to the 'Domain Admins' group
Right-click 'DHCP' in the console and select 'Manage Authorized Servers' to add the DC
Run 'ipconfig /registerdns'
Disable IPv6 on the server

tickets.title: Cross-VLAN Lease Failure
tickets.summary: Users in the new Branch office (VLAN 20) are getting 169.254.x.x addresses. Users in the HQ (VLAN 10), where the DHCP server is located, are working fine.
artifact: Router: Inter-VLAN routing is enabled; static IPs on VLAN 20 can ping the server.
DHCP Server: Scope for 10.10.20.0 exists and is active.
validations: Verify DHCP Discover packets reach the server from VLAN 20.
Check Router configuration for IP Helper-Address.
tickets.debrief: DHCP 'Discover' packets are Layer 2 broadcasts. Since routers are designed to block broadcasts, the requests from VLAN 20 never reach the server in VLAN 10. An 'IP Helper' or 'Relay Agent' on the router converts that broadcast into a unicast packet directed at the server's IP.

triage.q: How do you verify if the server is even seeing the requests from the remote Branch office?
options: Check the 'Address Leases' of the HQ scope
Check the DHCP Server Statistics or run a Packet Capture for 'Discovers' from the 10.10.20.x range
Check if the server's CPU usage is high
Ping the Branch office gateway from the server

diagnosis.q: The Packet Capture shows zero traffic from VLAN 20. Routing is working for static IPs. What is the bottleneck?
options: The DHCP server is too slow to respond
The Router is not configured to relay DHCP broadcasts across the VLAN boundary
The Branch scope has the wrong subnet mask
The DHCP server needs a physical NIC in every VLAN

fix.q: What is the industry-standard fix for this multi-VLAN architecture?
options: Configure an 'IP Helper-Address' (DHCP Relay) on the VLAN 20 gateway interface
Create a 'Superscope' on the DHCP server
Enable 'Promiscuous Mode' on the server NIC
Move the DHCP server to the Branch office

tickets.title: The 'BAD_ADDRESS' Conflict
tickets.summary: The DHCP console is filling up with 'BAD_ADDRESS' entries in the leases. Users are intermittently reporting 'IP Address Conflict' errors on their screens.
artifact: Console: Multiple 'BAD_ADDRESS' entries in the active scope.
Recent Change: 10 new network printers were installed with manual static IPs.
Symptom: Users cannot get an IP if the 'BAD_ADDRESS' count is high.
validations: Identify static IP range on printers.
Clear BAD_ADDRESS entries and monitor for recurrence.
tickets.debrief: The DHCP server uses 'Conflict Detection' (pings an IP before offering it). If something responds, it marks it 'BAD_ADDRESS' to prevent two devices from having the same IP. This usually happens when static IPs are assigned within the dynamic pool without setting an 'Exclusion.'

triage.q: What does a 'BAD_ADDRESS' entry actually tell you about the DHCP server's behavior?
options: The database is corrupted
The server attempted to offer the IP, but detected another device already using it (Conflict Detection)
The client has a malformed MAC address
The IP is blocked by the Windows Firewall

diagnosis.q: Given the recent printer installation, why is the server attempting to issue these 'BAD' IPs?
options: The printers are sending rogue DHCP offers
The printers were assigned static IPs that fall within the dynamic 'Address Pool' of the scope
The lease duration is too short
The DHCP database needs to be compacted

fix.q: What is the best way to prevent these conflicts permanently?
options: Disable Conflict Detection on the server
Configure 'Address Exclusions' for the range used by static devices like printers
Increase the lease duration to 30 days
Tell users to ignore the conflict popups
